prompts.ask: Which customers have an overdue invoice and an open urgent ticket right now?
prompts.reply: {n} customers are in that spot. The ones at the top have the most money outstanding, so I'd start there. Click any row to open the customer, then Draft reminder if you want to chase the invoice.
prompts.sql:
SELECT c.id, c.name, c.region, p.name AS plan,
       COUNT(DISTINCT i.id) AS overdue_invoices,
       ROUND(SUM(DISTINCT i.amount), 2) AS amount_overdue,
       COUNT(DISTINCT t.id) AS urgent_open,
       MIN(substr(t.opened_at, 1, 10)) AS oldest_urgent
FROM customers c
JOIN plans p ON p.id = c.plan_id
JOIN invoices i ON i.customer_id = c.id AND i.status = 'overdue'
JOIN tickets t ON t.customer_id = c.id AND t.priority = 'urgent' AND t.status IN ('open', 'pending', 'escalated')
WHERE c.churned_at IS NULL
GROUP BY c.id
ORDER BY amount_overdue DESC
LIMIT 50

result.sql:
SELECT c.id, c.name, c.region, p.name AS plan,
       COUNT(DISTINCT i.id) AS overdue_invoices,
       ROUND(SUM(DISTINCT i.amount), 2) AS amount_overdue,
       COUNT(DISTINCT t.id) AS urgent_open,
       MIN(substr(t.opened_at, 1, 10)) AS oldest_urgent
FROM customers c
JOIN plans p ON p.id = c.plan_id
JOIN invoices i ON i.customer_id = c.id AND i.status = 'overdue'
JOIN tickets t ON t.customer_id = c.id AND t.priority = 'urgent' AND t.status IN ('open', 'pending', 'escalated')
WHERE c.churned_at IS NULL
GROUP BY c.id
ORDER BY amount_overdue DESC
LIMIT 50

prompts.ask: How are tickets spread across category and priority this quarter, and how long do they take to resolve?
prompts.reply: This quarter's tickets by category and priority, with resolution time and CSAT for each. Use the chips to narrow to one priority, or sort by hours to see what sits longest.
prompts.sql:
SELECT category, priority,
       COUNT(*) AS tickets,
       SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'resolved' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS resolved,
       ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN resolved_at IS NOT NULL THEN (julianday(resolved_at) - julianday(opened_at)) * 24 END), 1) AS avg_hours_to_resolve,
       ROUND(AVG(csat), 2) AS avg_csat
FROM tickets
WHERE opened_at >= '2026-07-01'
GROUP BY category, priority
ORDER BY tickets DESC

result.sql:
SELECT category, priority,
       COUNT(*) AS tickets,
       SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'resolved' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS resolved,
       ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN resolved_at IS NOT NULL THEN (julianday(resolved_at) - julianday(opened_at)) * 24 END), 1) AS avg_hours_to_resolve,
       ROUND(AVG(csat), 2) AS avg_csat
FROM tickets
WHERE opened_at >= '2026-07-01'
GROUP BY category, priority
ORDER BY tickets DESC

prompts.ask: Which agents are carrying the most open escalated tickets, and how are their CSAT scores?
prompts.reply: Open and escalated tickets per agent, with each agent's average CSAT on resolved work. The load is uneven. Sort by escalated to see who needs help first.
prompts.sql:
SELECT a.name AS agent, a.team,
       SUM(CASE WHEN t.status IN ('open', 'pending') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS open_tickets,
       SUM(CASE WHEN t.status = 'escalated' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS escalated,
       ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN t.status = 'resolved' THEN t.csat END), 2) AS avg_csat,
       COUNT(*) AS all_time
FROM agents a
LEFT JOIN tickets t ON t.agent_id = a.id
GROUP BY a.id
ORDER BY escalated DESC, open_tickets DESC

result.sql:
SELECT a.name AS agent, a.team,
       SUM(CASE WHEN t.status IN ('open', 'pending') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS open_tickets,
       SUM(CASE WHEN t.status = 'escalated' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS escalated,
       ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN t.status = 'resolved' THEN t.csat END), 2) AS avg_csat,
       COUNT(*) AS all_time
FROM agents a
LEFT JOIN tickets t ON t.agent_id = a.id
GROUP BY a.id
ORDER BY escalated DESC, open_tickets DESC

prompts.ask: Show me paid revenue by region and plan for 2026.
prompts.reply: 2026 paid revenue by region and plan, {n} combinations. The chart groups by region; switch it to plan or flip to the table for the exact numbers.
prompts.sql:
SELECT c.region, p.name AS plan,
       COUNT(DISTINCT c.id) AS customers,
       COUNT(i.id) AS invoices,
       ROUND(SUM(i.amount), 2) AS revenue
FROM invoices i
JOIN customers c ON c.id = i.customer_id
JOIN plans p ON p.id = c.plan_id
WHERE i.status = 'paid' AND i.paid_at >= '2026-01-01'
GROUP BY c.region, p.name
ORDER BY revenue DESC

result.sql:
SELECT c.region, p.name AS plan,
       COUNT(DISTINCT c.id) AS customers,
       COUNT(i.id) AS invoices,
       ROUND(SUM(i.amount), 2) AS revenue
FROM invoices i
JOIN customers c ON c.id = i.customer_id
JOIN plans p ON p.id = c.plan_id
WHERE i.status = 'paid' AND i.paid_at >= '2026-01-01'
GROUP BY c.region, p.name
ORDER BY revenue DESC

prompts.ask: What does paid revenue look like month by month over the last twelve months?
prompts.reply: Monthly paid revenue for the trailing twelve months, with the number of invoices behind each bar. Sort the table by month to read it in order.
prompts.sql:
SELECT substr(paid_at, 1, 7) AS month,
       COUNT(*) AS invoices,
       ROUND(SUM(amount), 2) AS revenue
FROM invoices
WHERE status = 'paid' AND paid_at >= date('2026-10-25', '-12 months')
GROUP BY month
ORDER BY month

result.sql:
SELECT substr(paid_at, 1, 7) AS month,
       COUNT(*) AS invoices,
       ROUND(SUM(amount), 2) AS revenue
FROM invoices
WHERE status = 'paid' AND paid_at >= date('2026-10-25', '-12 months')
GROUP BY month
ORDER BY month

prompts.ask: How much is overdue right now, by region?
prompts.reply: Overdue invoices by region: how many, how much, and how old the oldest one is. The chart shows the dollar amount; flip to the table for the counts.
prompts.sql:
SELECT c.region,
       COUNT(i.id) AS overdue_invoices,
       COUNT(DISTINCT c.id) AS customers,
       ROUND(SUM(i.amount), 2) AS amount_overdue,
       MIN(substr(i.due_at, 1, 10)) AS oldest_due
FROM invoices i
JOIN customers c ON c.id = i.customer_id
WHERE i.status = 'overdue'
GROUP BY c.region
ORDER BY amount_overdue DESC

result.sql:
SELECT c.region,
       COUNT(i.id) AS overdue_invoices,
       COUNT(DISTINCT c.id) AS customers,
       ROUND(SUM(i.amount), 2) AS amount_overdue,
       MIN(substr(i.due_at, 1, 10)) AS oldest_due
FROM invoices i
JOIN customers c ON c.id = i.customer_id
WHERE i.status = 'overdue'
GROUP BY c.region
ORDER BY amount_overdue DESC

prompts.ask: Who are our 20 biggest customers by lifetime paid revenue, and do any of them have open tickets?
prompts.reply: Your top 20 by lifetime paid revenue. The open_tickets column shows who has something unresolved right now, and avg_csat is their average rating, so a low number next to a big account is worth a call.
prompts.sql:
SELECT c.id, c.name, c.industry, c.region, p.name AS plan,
       ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN i.status = 'paid' THEN i.amount ELSE 0 END), 2) AS paid_revenue,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tickets t WHERE t.customer_id = c.id AND t.status IN ('open', 'pending', 'escalated')) AS open_tickets,
       (SELECT ROUND(AVG(csat), 1) FROM tickets t WHERE t.customer_id = c.id AND csat IS NOT NULL) AS avg_csat
FROM customers c
JOIN plans p ON p.id = c.plan_id
JOIN invoices i ON i.customer_id = c.id
GROUP BY c.id
ORDER BY paid_revenue DESC
LIMIT 20

result.sql:
SELECT c.id, c.name, c.industry, c.region, p.name AS plan,
       ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN i.status = 'paid' THEN i.amount ELSE 0 END), 2) AS paid_revenue,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tickets t WHERE t.customer_id = c.id AND t.status IN ('open', 'pending', 'escalated')) AS open_tickets,
       (SELECT ROUND(AVG(csat), 1) FROM tickets t WHERE t.customer_id = c.id AND csat IS NOT NULL) AS avg_csat
FROM customers c
JOIN plans p ON p.id = c.plan_id
JOIN invoices i ON i.customer_id = c.id
GROUP BY c.id
ORDER BY paid_revenue DESC
LIMIT 20

prompts.ask: Which customers churned in the last six months, and what were they paying us?
prompts.reply: {n} customers churned since April. Lifetime paid is what we lost; the CSAT and ticket columns hint at why. Click one to see what their last few tickets were about.
prompts.sql:
SELECT c.id, c.name, c.industry, c.region, p.name AS plan,
       substr(c.churned_at, 1, 10) AS churned,
       ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN i.status = 'paid' THEN i.amount ELSE 0 END), 2) AS lifetime_paid,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tickets t WHERE t.customer_id = c.id) AS tickets,
       (SELECT ROUND(AVG(csat), 1) FROM tickets t WHERE t.customer_id = c.id AND csat IS NOT NULL) AS avg_csat
FROM customers c
JOIN plans p ON p.id = c.plan_id
LEFT JOIN invoices i ON i.customer_id = c.id
WHERE c.churned_at >= '2026-04-25'
GROUP BY c.id
ORDER BY lifetime_paid DESC

result.sql:
SELECT c.id, c.name, c.industry, c.region, p.name AS plan,
       substr(c.churned_at, 1, 10) AS churned,
       ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN i.status = 'paid' THEN i.amount ELSE 0 END), 2) AS lifetime_paid,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tickets t WHERE t.customer_id = c.id) AS tickets,
       (SELECT ROUND(AVG(csat), 1) FROM tickets t WHERE t.customer_id = c.id AND csat IS NOT NULL) AS avg_csat
FROM customers c
JOIN plans p ON p.id = c.plan_id
LEFT JOIN invoices i ON i.customer_id = c.id
WHERE c.churned_at >= '2026-04-25'
GROUP BY c.id
ORDER BY lifetime_paid DESC

prompts.ask: Which Team-plan customers are near their seat limit and have no open tickets? Those are my upsell calls.
prompts.reply: {n} Team-plan accounts are at 80% or more of their seat limit with nothing open in support. Sorted by how full they are. Good list for a Friday.
prompts.sql:
SELECT c.id, c.name, c.industry, c.region, c.seats, p.seat_limit,
       ROUND(100.0 * c.seats / p.seat_limit, 0) AS pct_of_limit,
       substr(c.created_at, 1, 10) AS customer_since
FROM customers c
JOIN plans p ON p.id = c.plan_id
WHERE p.name = 'Team' AND c.churned_at IS NULL AND p.seat_limit IS NOT NULL
  AND c.seats >= 0.8 * p.seat_limit
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM tickets t WHERE t.customer_id = c.id AND t.status IN ('open', 'pending', 'escalated'))
ORDER BY pct_of_limit DESC, c.seats DESC
LIMIT 50

result.sql:
SELECT c.id, c.name, c.industry, c.region, c.seats, p.seat_limit,
       ROUND(100.0 * c.seats / p.seat_limit, 0) AS pct_of_limit,
       substr(c.created_at, 1, 10) AS customer_since
FROM customers c
JOIN plans p ON p.id = c.plan_id
WHERE p.name = 'Team' AND c.churned_at IS NULL AND p.seat_limit IS NOT NULL
  AND c.seats >= 0.8 * p.seat_limit
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM tickets t WHERE t.customer_id = c.id AND t.status IN ('open', 'pending', 'escalated'))
ORDER BY pct_of_limit DESC, c.seats DESC
LIMIT 50
